quote: the proposal concerning the Macedonian war was rejected by almost all the tribes
notes: War-weary centuriate assembly, egged on by tribune Q. Baebius, rejects the senate's proposed declaration of war on Philip; senate rebukes the tribune and orders a new assembly (livy:en:31:6).

quote: After this speech of Sulpicius, being sent to give their votes, they declared for the war as he had proposed
notes: Re-vote after Sulpicius's speech in the Campus Martius reverses the earlier popular rejection and the centuries declare war on Philip (livy:en:31:8; speech in livy:en:31:7).

quote: but he was not empowered to take with him any veteran soldier against his will
notes: Reflecting veterans' resistance to re-enlistment after the Punic war, the senate restricts Sulpicius to volunteers from Scipio's returned African army and orders the veteran troops disbanded (livy:en:31:8).

quote: The pontiffs determined, that it could; and that it would be even more in order to do it in that way
notes: After the chief pontiff Licinius blocks the people's vow of games for the Macedonian war over funding, the pontifical college sanctions the first votive games vowed at an unspecified expense, a new religious-fiscal precedent (livy:en:31:9).

quote: appoint ten commissioners to survey, and distribute among them, that part of the Samnite and Apulian lands which was the property of the Roman people
notes: Senate decrees ager publicus in Samnium and Apulia for Scipio's African veterans and has the urban praetor name ten land commissioners; a land-settlement measure rather than agitation, hence the loose type fit (livy:en:31:4).

quote: a vast quantity of corn, which Scipio had sent from Africa, was distributed by them to the people
notes: Curule aediles distribute African grain sent by Scipio at four asses a peck; a subsidized distribution easing post-war food pressure rather than a scarcity crisis proper (livy:en:31:4).

quote: if they wished for peace, they must recall him, and give him up to the Roman people
notes: After the Gallic revolt and sack of Placentia, the senate sends an embassy demanding Carthage recall and surrender Hamilcar, the Carthaginian leading the Gauls; Carthage answers with exile and confiscation (quote at livy:en:31:11; answer at livy:en:31:19).

quote: the people were particularly shocked at the hermaphrodites, which were ordered to be immediately thrown into the sea
notes: Mass religious alarm at prodigies (hermaphrodites, monstrous births) is expiated by decemviral rites, a hymn by thrice nine virgins, and an offering to Juno; coded loosely as popular tumult since the codebook has no prodigy-expiation type (livy:en:31:12).

quote: that an inquiry be made concerning the robbery of the treasury, according to the method used by Marcus Pomponius
notes: Senate orders the praetor in Bruttium to hold a formal inquiry into the theft from Proserpine's treasury at Locri on the Pleminius-era model; money is restored out of the effects of the guilty (quote at livy:en:31:12; outcome at livy:en:31:13).

quote: they should, therefore, have liberty to purchase any belonging to the public, and which lay within fifty miles of the city
notes: With the treasury empty for the new war, creditors owed the third installment of Punic-war loans protest confiscation by stealth; the senate's compromise assigns ager publicus within fifty miles at a nominal one-as rent (the trientabula) (livy:en:31:13).

quote: Against this, Tiberius Sempronius Longus, tribune of the people, protested
notes: Senate refuses proconsul Lentulus a triumph for Spain for lack of precedent and grants an ovation; tribune Sempronius Longus vetoes even that, then withdraws under unanimous senatorial pressure (livy:en:31:20).

quote: The elder part refused him a triumph, both because the army, with which he had acted, belonged to another
notes: Praetor Furius, rushing to Rome in the consul's absence, demands a triumph for his Gallic victory; after a divided senate debate he prevails and triumphs in office, and consul Aurelius later protests the unprecedented procedure (debate at livy:en:31:48; see 31:47 and 31:49); coded as the nearest type for an intra-elite honors contest.

quote: he should, for every year, receive two acres; and that ten commissioners should distribute that land
notes: Senate fixes the veteran settlement at two iugera per year served in Spain or Africa, to be distributed by the ten commissioners; implementation of the land grant decreed at 31:4 (livy:en:31:49).

quote: Three commissioners were then appointed to fill up the number of colonists at Venusia
notes: Triumviral commission enrolls supplementary colonists for Venusia, depleted in the Hannibalic war; a colony reinforcement rather than a new foundation (livy:en:31:49).

quote: distributed among the people a vast quantity of corn, brought from Africa, at the rate of two asses a peck
notes: In a year of remarkably cheap provisions the curule aediles distribute African grain at two asses a peck; abundance-driven distribution, not scarcity (livy:en:31:50).

quote: being flamen Dialis, could not take the oath of observing the laws; and no person was allowed to hold any office longer than five days
notes: Curule aedile-elect C. Valerius Flaccus, as flamen Dialis, cannot swear the magistrate's oath; senate, tribunes, and a plebiscite allow his brother to swear by proxy, and a parallel plebiscite recalls his absent colleague Cethegus from Spain (livy:en:31:50).
